name: Incline Dumbbell Triceps Extension
summary: An isolation exercise performed on an incline bench that targets the triceps brachii with an emphasized stretch on the long head.

setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of approximately 30 to 45 degrees.
Sit back firmly against the pad with feet flat on the floor.
Raise a pair of dumbbells overhead with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), extending your arms so the upper arms are angled slightly back past perpendicular to your torso.
steps: Keep your upper arms stationary and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells in a controlled arc behind your head.
Lower until your elbows reach approximately 90 degrees or you feel a deep stretch in your triceps.
Extend your elbows smoothly by contracting your triceps to return the dumbbells to the starting position without locking out aggressively.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the weights behind your head and exhale as you extend your elbows to return to the top.
cues: Keep your elbows pointed forward, not flared wide.
Pin your upper arms in place; move only the forearms.
Control the descent for a full triceps stretch.

common_faults.correction: Keep elbows aligned roughly shoulder-width apart to keep tension on the triceps and reduce stress on the shoulder joint.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the upper arms forward and back to gain momentum.
common_faults.correction: Lock the shoulders into a stable angle and isolate movement strictly to the elbow joint.

precautions: Use a manageable load to avoid accidental contact with the head or overstraining the elbow tendons.
